info.name: Connectum: mobile QR and join flow
info.description:
Everything the mobile app calls for a scanned QR code: the public lookups, account sign-in, join and enter, and the code actions. See docs/MOBILE_QR.md.

Three values are used in every handoff, with the same names: **code**, **org**, **branch**.

| Handoff | Form |
|---|---|
| Link | `https://connectum.app/connect/{CODE}[?org={ORG}][&branch={name}]` |
| Open in Connectum | `connectum://connect/{CODE}[?org=..][&branch=..]` |
| Android Play referrer | `connect_code={CODE}[&connect_org=..][&connect_branch=..]` |
| iPhone clipboard | `connectum:{CODE}[?org=..][&branch=..]` |

Defaults: the test organisation 'Test organisation Mobile team' (Y2NHGHP6), which has the branches Head office and Testing.

## Updated 2 November 2026
Folder 5 lists what changed for the mobile app: end-to-end encryption recovery (a new device flagged `recovery`, three new actions), approvals (`canRespond`, nobody answers their own request, who answered), hidden form fields whose value is made for the person (still sent), password sign-in, showing the earlier messages on a new device (four new actions and a box that may carry its own `ek`), the backup and restore for the recovery code, message formatting and message options (no request changed), save and pin and mark as unread, the older-device side of the history sync (vectors, a stand-in new device, exact rules) and the form logic for the mobile app. Start with docs/MOBILE_HANDOVER.md in the repository. Real replies from a running server.

item.name: 1. Public (no sign-in)
item.description: What a phone can ask before anyone signs in. 60 requests a minute per address, shared by these calls and the landing page.

request.description: The page a scanned **organisation** QR opens (HTML). `branch` is shown only when the organisation really has it. With the app installed and the app-link files set, a phone opens the app instead.

The organisation's public card: name, location, QR payload, the categories it offers joiners.

item.name: A person's link: the organisation's card only

request.description:
A person's code with `org`: the card of the organisation `org` names, `fromPersonLink: true`. The person's code is NOT looked at, so a real code and a made-up one answer alike. `org` is the organisation's public code. A person's link carries it; an organisation's own link does not need it (one in it is ignored).

The whole link may also be passed as the code (URL-encoded), e.g. `https%3A%2F%2Fconnectum.app%2Fconnect%2FKVZDHDQD%3Forg%3DY2NHGHP6`, or `connectum://connect/CODE?org=..`.

item.name: 4. Codes (WebSocket /sd actions)
item.description:
These run over the WebSocket after `enter` (Postman cannot keep a WebSocket request inside a collection run, so each is shown as its message). A code may be written as the whole link, `connectum:CODE`, `{scheme}://connect/CODE` (with or without `?org=` and `?branch=`), `CODE?org=..`, or the bare code. Limit: `connect.lookup` and `connect.scan` share 60 tries per 10 minutes per person.

If the link names **another organisation** than the one the person is in, both answer `wrong_org` and connect nobody.

item.name: connect.my: my code and the organisation's

request.description:
**WebSocket message** (open a WebSocket request to `wss://connectum.app/ws`, send `{"username":"<username>","token":"{{token}}"}` first, wait for `welcome`, then send):

```
/sd connect.my {"reqId":"1"}
```

The person's own code and the organisation's, with the `payload` text to draw as a QR. The person's payload carries `?org=`.

Or from a terminal: `WS=wss://connectum.app/ws USERNAME=<username> TOKEN=<token> node tools/postman/sd-call.mjs connect.my '{}'`

item.name: 5. What changed for the mobile app (read this first)
item.description: What changed for the mobile app on 1 November 2026, with real replies from a running server. The WebSocket requests are shown as their message (Postman cannot keep a WebSocket request inside a collection run). The full reference is in the main collection (Connectum.postman_collection.json, folder 4) and docs/E2E_ENCRYPTION.md.

item.name: What changed, and what the mobile app must do

request.description:
Twelve changes since the last version of this collection. Nothing was removed or renamed; what is new is additive except where it says **must**.

**1. End-to-end encryption: recovery (new, optional for the person).** A person can turn on a recovery key. It is registered as one more device with `recovery: true` in `e2e.status` and `e2e.devices`. The app **must** wrap every message for it like for any other device it is given (it already does, if it wraps for every device in the list), must not offer to remove it as a device, and should not show it among "your devices" (`e2e.remove` refuses it). New actions: `e2e.recovery.set`, `e2e.recovery.get`, `e2e.recovery.delete`. Recovery covers messages sent after it is turned on; see docs/E2E_ENCRYPTION.md section 6a for the code format, the sealing (HKDF-SHA-256, AES-256-GCM) and the limits. The mobile app needs the screens: turn on and show the code once, enter a code on a new phone, make a new code, turn off.

**2. Approvals: nobody answers their own request (changed rule).** `req.list` gives each request `canRespond` and `direction`: show Approve and Decline **only when `canRespond` is true**. It is false for the person who sent the request, an administrator included. `req.respond` on your own request is refused with `forbidden`. If the app showed the buttons for administrators before, it must stop.

**3. Approvals: who answered (new fields).** An answered request carries `resolvedBy`, `resolvedByName` and `resolvedByDesignation`. The card tag next to the applicant's name is now the **designation of the person who answered** (for example Manager) instead of the applicant's category; keep the applicant's category while it is still waiting. Fall back to the category when `resolvedByDesignation` is null.

**4. Forms: a hidden field whose value is made for the person (changed rule).** A field may be hidden (`hidden: true`). Before, nothing was saved for a hidden field. Now: for a field that works itself out (`calc`), fills itself (`fetch`) or is an Auto Generate number, `hidden` only keeps it **off the screen**: the app must still work out the `calc` value, and **send it** with `tstruct.submit` (and with an edit); the server checks and saves it. For any other hidden field, whatever is sent is ignored, as before. A hidden field is never asked of the person and never counts as required on the screen.

**5. Password sign-in (already there, now listed).** `login/password` and the `account/password/*` calls are in folder 2.

**9. End-to-end: a new device is shown the earlier messages by a device the person already uses (new; the app must add it).** Today a device added later cannot open what was sent before. Now a device the person already uses opens each message with its own key and locks the message key again for the new device; the server adds those boxes, for that device only, when it serves the message. The person approves in the app on the older device ("Show your earlier messages on <device>?"). **Two things the app must do:** (a) **reading:** a box may carry its own one-time key, `keys[<device>].ek`: when it is there, use it instead of the envelope's `ek` for the key agreement; (b) **handing on:** `e2e.status` gives each device `late`; `e2e.sync.pending` lists waiting devices; the app shows the offer, then for each message from `e2e.sync.page` (or from its own stored envelopes) makes a box for the waiting device and sends batches with `e2e.sync.put`, then `e2e.sync.done`. Everything is described, with the algorithm, the edge cases and a reference message, in `docs/E2E_HISTORY_SYNC_MOBILE.md`. Note: one active session per person: signing in on the older device signs the new one out until it has finished; the new device signs in again afterwards.

**10. End-to-end: backup and restore for the recovery code (new; the app must add it).** WhatsApp's encrypted backup, with no file in a cloud. When a person turns recovery on, a device locks the **earlier** messages for the **recovery key** too (the same job as showing the past to a new device, with the recovery key's id as the target of `e2e.sync.put`, then `e2e.sync.done`). On a new device the person types the code; the app opens everything with the recovery key and locks the past **for this device** (source = the recovery key, target = this device), so it no longer needs the code. `e2e.sync.pending` now has `recovery: null | {id, backedUp}`; `e2e.status` lists the recovery key with `late: true` until its backup is complete; `e2e.sync.put` accepts any of the person's own devices, the recovery key included. Details, the algorithm and edge cases: `docs/E2E_HISTORY_SYNC_MOBILE.md`, section Backup and restore.

**11. Message formatting (the web app draws it; the mobile app should too; no API changed).** A message is still plain text: nothing changed in any request or reply, and the server keeps every line break, tab and blank line exactly. The web app now draws a small Markdown (`**bold**`, `_italic_`, `~~strike~~`, `` `code` ``, fenced code blocks, `> quote`, `- bullets`, `1. numbers` nested by indentation, `[words](https://link)` and bare links) with line breaks and indentation as typed, and shows previews as one plain line. `docs/MESSAGE_FORMATTING.md` has the rules, and `docs/message-format-vectors.json` has 32 sample messages with the exact result, to check a parser against. Send the text as typed (the end of the whole message is trimmed; at most 2000 characters).

**12. Message options and a link to a message (web app; no API changed).** The web app has a Teams-style bar over a message (four quick reactions, more emoji, edit for your own, more) and a menu (reply with quote, forward, copy text, copy link, edit, delete). **Copy link** gives `https://<the app>/?chat=<chat>&msg=<message id>` (`<chat>` is `user-<name>`, `room-<group>`, `room-general` or `host-<key>`): the web app opens that chat and flashes the message, and the mobile app can share and open the same link. Only the author edits or deletes. Described in `docs/MESSAGE_OPTIONS.md`.

**13. Save, pin and mark as unread (new; the app can add them).** Three more options in the message menu. **Save** is private: `msg.save {conv, id}`, `msg.unsave {id}`, `msg.saved {limit?, offset?}` (newest saved first; `{ids:true}` returns only the ids to mark messages in a chat); at most 500 per person; the person's other devices get `saved_changed`. **Pin** is for everyone in a direct chat or group (not the general room): `msg.pin {conv, id}`, `msg.unpin`, `msg.pins {conv}`; either person or any member may pin or unpin; at most 10 per conversation (`limit` says so in words); everyone in the conversation gets `pins_changed {conv, id, pinned, by}` (ask `msg.pins` again). **Mark as unread:** `conv.unread {id, messageId}` sets `unreadFrom` on the conversation (my own view only, the other person's receipts do not change); `unread` counts from there; the next `conv.read` clears it. `conv` is `dm:<user>`, `group:<name>` or `global`; the text of an end-to-end message comes back narrowed to the person's own boxes like any history, so open it as usual. A message deleted for everyone leaves both lists. Described in `docs/MESSAGE_OPTIONS.md` and `docs/SD_ACTIONS_REFERENCE.md`; real replies are in the worked examples below.

**14. The older-device side of change 9: vectors, a stand-in new device, exact rules (docs and tools; no API changed).** `docs/E2E_HISTORY_SYNC_MOBILE.md` now has the exact rewrap, test vectors with fixed inputs (`docs/e2e-test-vectors.json` → `rewrap`: the expected `{mid, iv, w, ek}` and the boxes that must be refused), full real replies of both roles (`docs/e2e-sync-replies.json`), the rules for `e2e.sync.put` and `done` (the same `mid` twice is safe, a bad item refuses the whole call, any device of the person is accepted), the one-session behaviour, and `tools/e2e-kit/new-device.mjs`, a stand-in for the new device, so the older-device side can be tested with one phone. Failures of `e2e.sync.put` are not per item: see the examples below.

**15. Form logic for the mobile app (files, docs and sample forms; no API changed).** The form logic the web runs is published as plain files with a version and SHA-256: `GET /form-logic/manifest.json` (and `axExpParser.js`, `fieldRule.js`, `fieldCalc.js`, `axFunctions.js` beside it): bundle a copy, fetch a newer one when `version` goes up, check every hash. `Date()` is now today where the person is (it was the UTC date: yesterday in India until 5:30). A switch is saved as Yes or No, and a condition on Yes is now met by `true` and the other spellings. The server never runs `rule` or `calc`; it checks the shape of each value. The files include a one-script bundle (`form-logic.bundle.js`, global `ConnectumFormLogic`), a host shim for small engines and a conformance file to run in your engine (tested in JavaScriptCore and a bare engine). `tstruct.get` now returns `rev` (a fingerprint of the saved form) and `form.options` returns `etag` and `cacheSec` and takes `ifNoneMatch` (answered `notModified`), for offline caching. Docs: `docs/FORM_LOGIC_FOR_MOBILE.md` (the files, what the engine needs, grid cells, what the server checks, offline choices), `docs/FORM_FIELD_TYPES.md` (every field type and the value it is saved as), `docs/sample-forms/` (twelve sample forms, one per feature, `node tools/sample-forms/load.mjs`, and `cases.json` with the numbers to expect).

**8. A new device on the account is announced to its owner (new, nothing to change in the app).** When a second (or later) device is added to a person's encrypted messaging, the notification feed gets an item on every device they have: `category: "security"`, `severity: "medium"`, title "A new device was added to your encrypted messages", `message` naming the device. It is not made for a person's first device, for the same device registering again, or for the recovery key. Show it like any feed item; there is no new event, action or field. Optional: tell the person once when a contact you already know gets a new device (you already pin devices): skip your own devices and `recovery: true` ones. Details: docs/E2E_MOBILE_REVIEW.md, last section.

**7. End-to-end: a message must have a box for EVERY device that exists now (new, enforced by the server).** Before, the server accepted a message with a box for at least one device of each person, so a sender with an old list left a new phone or browser unable to read it ("Sent before this browser was set up for encryption"). Now a message that misses a device, or has a box for a device that no longer exists, is refused with `e2e_stale_devices` and nothing is stored or delivered. The sending device itself may leave its own box out. **What the app must do:** ask `e2e.devices` right before encrypting each message (the sender's own other devices too), and on `e2e_stale_devices` look up the devices of `users` again, make a **new** envelope from the same text and send it again, by itself, without telling the person; match the refusal to your message by `mid`. Direct chat is what matters for mobile now; the same rule applies to group envelopes. Details: docs/E2E_FRESH_DEVICES_CHANGE.md. Switch for the server: `CONNECTUM_E2E_REQUIRE_ALL_DEVICES=0` puts the old rule back.

**6. Faster file downloads (new, optional).** Ask `GET /api/sd/files/{id}/link` first. When `url` is a string, download the file from that address with a plain GET and **no Authorization header**: it is a short-lived (about a minute) link straight to the cloud store, so large files do not pass through our server. Save it under `name`. When `url` is `null`, or the download from the link fails for any reason (expired, no network to the store), use `GET /api/sd/files/{id}` as before: it has the same permission check. Never keep or share a link: ask again each time.

request.description:
**WebSocket message** (open a WebSocket request to `wss://connectum.app/ws`, send `{"username":"<username>","token":"{{token}}"}` first, wait for `welcome`, then send):

```
/msg <username> e2e1:{...an envelope with no box for one of their devices...}
```

The reply when the envelope leaves out a device that exists now (or has a box for one that is gone). Nothing was stored or delivered. `mid` is the `mid` of the envelope you sent, `conv` its conversation, `users` the people whose devices to look up again (`e2e.devices`). Build a NEW envelope from the same text and send it again, without telling the person. The example is the shape of the reply, not a captured one.
